testCases.testCaseName: Collection Barring - New Commands for Roaming Subscriber on 2G/3G
testCases.description: Verify that new collection barring commands are sent from AAM to NHLR for a roaming postpaid subscriber on 2G/3G network when IAR switch is ON and subscriber has outstanding balance
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Postpaid subscriber is active and currently roaming internationally
Subscriber is on 2G/3G network technology
Subscriber has outstanding balance exceeding threshold
Incoming SMS while roaming is enabled on network side
testSteps: Step 1: Identify a postpaid subscriber with outstanding balance currently roaming on 2G/3G network
Step 2: Trigger collection barring order from OMS for the subscriber
Step 3: Verify OMS sends the barring request to AAM without BB829 identifier
Step 4: Capture the command sent from AAM to NHLR
Step 5: Verify the command format matches the new barring command specification
Step 6: Verify the barring is applied successfully on the network
Step 7: Validate that the subscriber can still receive incoming SMS while roaming
testCases.expectedResults: New collection barring command is sent from AAM to NHLR. The subscriber is barred but can still receive incoming SMS and OTPs while roaming for mobile banking purposes. The barring command format matches the new specification defined in BPT.
testCases.relatedRequirement: IAR 829 - Section 2.1 - Collection Barring with New Commands

testCases.testCaseName: Migration Solution - Unbarring with BB829 Identifier for Pre-Deployment Barring
testCases.description: Verify that old unbarring commands are sent when unbarring a subscriber who was barred before IAR deployment using the BB829 identifier
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Postpaid subscriber was barred using old commands before IAR deployment
Subscriber barring order exists in the system from prior deployment
testSteps: Step 1: Identify a subscriber who was barred using old commands before IAR deployment
Step 2: Clear the outstanding balance or resolve the barring reason for the subscriber
Step 3: Trigger unbarring order from OMS for the subscriber
Step 4: Verify OMS includes the 'BB829' identifier in the reason code field
Step 5: Verify AAM receives the unbarring request with BB829 identifier
Step 6: Capture the command sent from AAM to NHLR
Step 7: Verify the command format matches the OLD unbarring command specification (not new)
Step 8: Verify the unbarring is applied successfully on the network
Step 9: Validate that there is no misalignment on the network side
testCases.expectedResults: OMS includes BB829 identifier in reason code. AAM sends OLD unbarring commands to NHLR. The subscriber is successfully unbarred without manual intervention and no network misalignment occurs.

Step 3: Verify OMS does NOT include 'BB829' identifier in the reason code field
Step 4: Verify AAM receives the barring request without BB829 identifier
Step 5: Capture the command sent from AAM to NHLR
Step 6: Verify the command format matches the NEW barring command specification
testCases.expectedResults: OMS does NOT include BB829 identifier for new barring orders. AAM sends NEW barring commands to NHLR as expected.

Payment gateway is operational
testSteps: Step 1: Customer is roaming abroad and barred for outstanding balance
Step 2: Customer makes full payment through mobile app/web
Step 3: Payment is processed and reflected in the billing system
Step 4: Automatic unbarring process is triggered
Step 5: Verify unbarring order is sent without BB829 identifier
Step 6: Verify new unbarring commands are sent from AAM to NHLR
Step 7: Customer receives notification of service restoration
Step 8: Customer verifies full service is restored while still roaming
testCases.expectedResults: After payment, the customer is automatically unbarred using new unbarring commands. Full service is restored seamlessly while the customer is still roaming abroad.
testCases.relatedRequirement: IAR 829 - Section 2.1 - Collection Unbarring with New Commands

testCases.testCaseName: UAT - End-to-End Collection Barring and Unbarring Lifecycle
testCases.description: Complete lifecycle UAT from barring to unbarring for a roaming customer with collection issues
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Postpaid customer is currently roaming abroad
Customer has active voice, SMS, and data services
Billing system is operational
testSteps: Step 1: Customer accumulates outstanding balance beyond threshold while roaming
Step 2: Collection system triggers barring order for the customer
Step 3: Verify new barring commands are sent from AAM to NHLR
Step 4: Verify customer is barred but can still receive incoming SMS
Step 5: Customer attempts outgoing voice call - verify it is blocked
Step 6: Customer receives OTP for online transaction - verify it is received
Step 7: Customer makes partial payment - verify barring status unchanged
Step 8: Customer makes full payment clearing outstanding balance
Step 9: Verify automatic unbarring is triggered with new commands
Step 10: Customer verifies all services are fully restored
testCases.expectedResults: Complete barring/unbarring lifecycle works seamlessly. Customer can receive SMS while barred. After payment, full service is restored using new commands.

testCases.testCaseName: Negative Test - Network SMS Prerequisite Not Met
testCases.description: Verify system behavior when incoming SMS while roaming is NOT enabled on network side
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Incoming SMS while roaming is NOT enabled on network side (prerequisite not met)
Postpaid subscriber is roaming and barred
testSteps: Step 1: Ensure incoming SMS while roaming is disabled on network side
Step 2: Trigger collection barring for a roaming subscriber
Step 3: Verify new barring commands are sent from AAM to NHLR
Step 4: Send an SMS to the barred roaming subscriber
Step 5: Observe the SMS delivery behavior
Step 6: Document the failure scenario
testCases.expectedResults: Even though AAM sends correct new barring commands, the subscriber cannot receive incoming SMS because the network prerequisite is not met. This validates the dependency on network configuration.
testCases.relatedRequirement: IAR 829 - Section 1.2 - Assumptions (Prerequisite for incoming SMS)

testCases.testCaseName: Negative Test - Mixed Old and New Commands Incompatibility
testCases.description: Verify that attempting to unbar with new commands when barring was done with old commands causes issues (validating the need for BB829)
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Subscriber was barred using old commands before IAR deployment
BB829 identifier is missing or corrupted in the unbarring request
testSteps: Step 1: Identify a subscriber barred with old commands before IAR deployment
Step 2: Simulate unbarring request without BB829 identifier (as if it's a new barring)
Step 3: Observe AAM sending new unbarring commands to NHLR
Step 4: Verify the network response to incompatible commands
Step 5: Document the error/failure behavior
Step 6: Verify subscriber remains barred or has partial service
testCases.expectedResults: When BB829 is missing for pre-deployment barred subscribers, new unbarring commands are sent which are incompatible with old barring. This results in failed unbarring or network misalignment, validating the importance of the BB829 migration solution.

testCases.testCaseName: Boundary Test - Subscriber at Exact Spending Limit Threshold
testCases.description: Verify system behavior when subscriber usage is exactly at the spending limit threshold
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Postpaid subscriber has a defined spending limit of X amount
Subscriber is currently roaming
testSteps: Step 1: Identify a roaming subscriber with spending limit of X
Step 2: Generate usage that brings subscriber to exactly X (at threshold, not exceeding)
Step 3: Verify if SL barring is triggered or not at exact threshold
Step 4: Generate additional minimal usage to exceed X by smallest increment
Step 5: Verify SL barring is triggered after exceeding threshold
Step 6: Verify new barring commands are sent from AAM to NHLR
Step 7: Verify subscriber can receive incoming SMS after barring
testCases.expectedResults: At exact threshold, barring may or may not trigger depending on business rules (document behavior). After exceeding threshold, SL barring is triggered with new commands. Incoming SMS works while barred.

testCases.testCaseName: Integration Test - AAM to NHLR Command Format Validation
testCases.description: Verify that the new command format from AAM to NHLR matches the specification provided by NTG
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
BPT with new commands has been gathered
Network side (NHLR) is ready to accept new commands
testSteps: Step 1: Review the new command specification from BPT
Step 2: Trigger a collection barring for a test subscriber
Step 3: Capture the exact command sent from AAM to NHLR
Step 4: Compare command format with BPT specification
Step 5: Verify all mandatory parameters are present and correctly formatted
Step 6: Verify command is accepted by NHLR without errors
Step 7: Repeat for unbarring command
Step 8: Repeat for all barring types (Collection, SL, Fraud in roaming)
testCases.expectedResults: All new commands from AAM exactly match the BPT specification. Commands are accepted by NHLR without parsing or format errors. Integration is successful.

testCases.testCaseName: Integration Test - OMS to AAM BB829 Identifier Transmission
testCases.description: Verify that OMS correctly transmits BB829 identifier to AAM in the reason code field
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Subscriber was barred before IAR deployment
OMS and AAM integration is operational
testSteps: Step 1: Identify a pre-deployment barred subscriber in OMS
Step 2: Initiate unbarring process through OMS
Step 3: Capture the request sent from OMS to AAM
Step 4: Verify 'BB829' is present in the reason code field
Step 5: Verify the exact format and position of BB829 identifier
Step 6: Verify AAM correctly parses and interprets the BB829 identifier
Step 7: Verify AAM triggers old unbarring commands based on BB829
testCases.expectedResults: OMS correctly includes BB829 in reason code field. AAM successfully parses and interprets BB829. Old unbarring commands are sent based on the identifier.

testCases.testCaseName: Regression Test - Other Flows Unchanged (BAU)
testCases.description: Verify that all other flows except collection, SL barring/unbarring and roaming fraud barring/unbarring continue to function as BAU
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Various non-impacted flows are available for testing
testSteps: Step 1: Test subscriber activation flow - verify BAU behavior
Step 2: Test subscriber suspension flow (non-collection) - verify BAU behavior
Step 3: Test plan change flow - verify BAU behavior
Step 4: Test add-on activation flow - verify BAU behavior
Step 5: Test billing flow - verify BAU behavior
Step 6: Test non-roaming fraud barring - verify existing commands (BAU)
Step 7: Document any deviations from expected BAU behavior
testCases.expectedResults: All non-impacted flows continue to function exactly as before IAR deployment. No regression is observed in any BAU functionality.

testCases.testCaseName: Regression Test - Collection and Service Barring Attributes Unchanged
testCases.description: Verify that existing collection and service barring attributes remain as per BAU
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Collection barring attributes are defined in system
Service barring attributes are defined in system
testSteps: Step 1: Review current collection barring attributes in system configuration
Step 2: Compare with pre-deployment collection barring attributes
Step 3: Verify no changes to collection barring attribute definitions
Step 4: Review current service barring attributes in system configuration
Step 5: Compare with pre-deployment service barring attributes
Step 6: Verify no changes to service barring attribute definitions
Step 7: Trigger a barring and verify attributes are applied as per BAU
testCases.expectedResults: All collection and service barring attributes remain unchanged from pre-deployment configuration. Attributes are applied consistently as per BAU.

testCases.testCaseName: UAT - International Subscriber Travels and Gets Barred While Roaming
testCases.description: Complete end-to-end UAT simulating a customer traveling abroad and getting barred for outstanding balance
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Postpaid customer with roaming service is identified
Customer has moderate outstanding balance
Incoming SMS while roaming is enabled on network
testSteps: Step 1: Customer departs from home country with phone in airplane mode
Step 2: Customer arrives at international destination
Step 3: Customer enables roaming on their device
Step 4: Verify customer registers on foreign network successfully
Step 5: Customer's outstanding balance exceeds threshold (or was already exceeded)
Step 6: Collection barring is triggered for the customer
Step 7: Verify new barring commands are processed
Step 8: Customer attempts to make an outgoing call - verify blocked
Step 9: Customer attempts to send SMS - verify blocked
Step 10: Someone sends SMS to customer - verify customer receives it
Step 11: Customer receives OTP from bank - verify successful receipt
Step 12: Customer completes banking transaction using OTP
testCases.expectedResults: Customer traveling abroad is properly barred but can receive incoming SMS including OTPs. The customer can continue using mobile banking for critical transactions despite being barred.

testCases.testCaseName: Performance Test - Multiple Concurrent Barring Operations
testCases.description: Verify system performance when multiple barring/unbarring operations are processed concurrently
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Load testing environment is set up
Multiple test subscribers are available
testSteps: Step 1: Prepare 100 test subscribers for concurrent barring
Step 2: Trigger simultaneous collection barring for all 100 subscribers
Step 3: Monitor system performance (response time, throughput)
Step 4: Verify all barring commands are sent correctly to NHLR
Step 5: Verify no command failures or timeouts occur
Step 6: Repeat for 100 concurrent unbarring operations
Step 7: Document performance metrics
testCases.expectedResults: System handles concurrent barring/unbarring operations efficiently. All commands are processed correctly without failures. Performance is within acceptable thresholds.

testCases.testCaseName: Negative Test - Order Initiated Before Deployment with New Commands
testCases.description: Verify that orders initiated before IAR deployment are handled correctly and new commands are not applied
preconditions: IAR 829 has just been deployed
There are pending barring orders initiated before deployment
testSteps: Step 1: Identify barring orders initiated before IAR deployment that are still pending
Step 2: Allow the pending orders to process post-deployment
Step 3: Verify the command type used for these orders
Step 4: Confirm old commands are used for pre-deployment initiated orders
Step 5: Verify no mixing of old and new commands occurs
testCases.expectedResults: Orders initiated before deployment use old commands even if processed after deployment. New commands are only used for orders initiated after deployment.

testCases.testCaseName: Technology Transition Test - Subscriber Moving Between 2G/3G and LTE While Barred
testCases.description: Verify barring behavior when subscriber transitions between network technologies while barred
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Postpaid subscriber is barred while roaming
Subscriber's device supports both 2G/3G and LTE
testSteps: Step 1: Subscriber is barred while connected to 2G/3G network while roaming
Step 2: Subscriber moves to an area with LTE coverage
Step 3: Device automatically switches to LTE network
Step 4: Verify barring status is maintained across technology change
Step 5: Verify incoming SMS capability is maintained on LTE
Step 6: Subscriber moves back to 2G/3G area
Step 7: Verify barring and SMS capability consistent across transition
testCases.expectedResults: Barring status is maintained consistently when subscriber transitions between 2G/3G and LTE. Incoming SMS capability remains functional across technology changes.

testCases.testCaseName: Risk Validation - Profile Misalignment for Pre-Deployment Barred Customers
testCases.description: Verify that proper migration solution prevents profile misalignment on network side for pre-deployment barred customers
preconditions: IAR 829 is deployed and switch is set to ON
Multiple subscribers were barred before IAR deployment
BB829 migration solution is active
testSteps: Step 1: Identify 10 subscribers barred before IAR deployment
Step 2: Capture their current network profile status from NHLR
Step 3: Trigger unbarring for all 10 subscribers
Step 4: Verify OMS includes BB829 for each unbarring request
Step 5: Verify AAM sends old unbarring commands
Step 6: Capture network profile status after unbarring
Step 7: Compare before and after profiles to verify proper restoration
Step 8: Verify no profile misalignment exists on network side
testCases.expectedResults: All pre-deployment barred customers are properly unbarred using old commands via BB829 solution. No profile misalignment occurs on NHLR. The risk identified in Section 13 is mitigated.
